ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.error: Orders words by the first letter only.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.cause: Stops comparing after the first letter.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.reveals: A question like "Order: bat, bag, ball" with "bat, bag, ball" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "bag, ball, bat", not "bat, bag, ball".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.feedback: When the first letters match, look at the second letter, then the third.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.error: Does not use the guide words to find the page.

example.question: Guide words "cat" and "cow": is "cup" on this page?

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.cause: Does not know guide words are the first and last words on the page.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.reveals: A question like "Guide words "cat" and "cow": is "cup" on this page?" with "Yes" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "No", not "Yes".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.feedback: Guide words show the first and last words on a page. A word is on the page only if it comes between them in alphabetical order.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.error: Picks a meaning that fits another sense of the word.

example.question: sprint
example.correct_answer: a very fast run for a short distance

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.cause: Chooses the first meaning that sounds familiar.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.reveals: A question like "sprint" with "a long walk" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a very fast run for a short distance", not "a long walk".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.feedback: Read all the meanings, then try each in the sentence to see which one fits.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.DICT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.error: Uses a dictionary to find facts about a topic.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.cause: Thinks every reference book does the same job.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.reveals: A question like "You want facts about elephants." with "a dictionary" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a junior encyclopaedia", not "a dictionary".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.feedback: A dictionary tells the meaning and spelling of words. A junior encyclopaedia gives facts about topics.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.error: Uses an atlas to find the meaning of a word.

example.question: You want to find a map of Kenya.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.cause: Does not link the book to what it holds.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.reveals: A question like "You want to find a map of Kenya." with "a dictionary" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "an atlas", not "a dictionary".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.feedback: An atlas is a book of maps. Use it to find places and countries.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.error: Uses a story book to look up information.

example.question: You want to know a bus time.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.cause: Thinks a book is good for any need.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.reveals: A question like "You want to know a bus time." with "a story book" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a timetable", not "a story book".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.feedback: A timetable lists times. A story book tells an invented story and is not for looking things up.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.error: Uses a newspaper for facts that do not change.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.cause: Does not think about when the information is needed.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.reveals: A question like "You want today's news." with "a dictionary" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a newspaper", not "a dictionary".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.feedback: A newspaper gives news of today. A dictionary or encyclopaedia gives facts that stay the same.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Writes a before a word that starts with a vowel sound.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Learns "a" as the only small word and does not listen to the first sound of the next word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "She ate ___ orange." with "a" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "an", not "a".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: Before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u) use "an": an orange, an egg.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Writes an before a word that starts with a consonant sound.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Over-corrects after learning that "an" goes before vowels.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "I bought ___ book." with "an" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a", not "an".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: Before a consonant sound use "a": a book, a pen.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Chooses a or an by the first letter, not the first sound.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Looks at the letter h (or u) instead of listening to the sound.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "We waited for ___ hour." with "a" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "an", not "a".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: Listen to the sound, not the letter. "Hour" starts with the sound "ow", so it takes "an". "Uniform" starts with the sound "yoo", so it takes "a".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Uses the for something that has not been mentioned before.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Thinks the is the main article.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "Mama gave me ___ apple." with "the" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "an", not "the".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: Use a or an the first time you speak about a thing. Use the when both people already know which one.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Uses a or an for something that is known or the only one.

example.question: We feel the heat of ___ sun.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Does not see that there is only one of it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "We feel the heat of ___ sun." with "a" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the", not "a".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: Use the for something that is the only one (the sun, the moon) or that both people know about.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Leaves out the article before a singular noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Kiswahili has no articles, so the small word is not heard as needed.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "Kamau has ___ new bicycle." with "no article" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a", not "no article".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: A singular thing you can count needs a, an or the before it: a new bicycle.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.error: Uses the for things in general, or uses a with a plural.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.cause: Believes "the" is needed before every noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.reveals: A question like "___ lions are strong animals." with "The" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "no article (Lions are strong animals.)", not "The".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.feedback: When you speak about a kind of thing in general, use no article: Lions are strong animals. Use "the" for one particular thing both people know.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_DETERMI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.error: Writes the wrong detail in a box.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.cause: Does not read what the box asks for.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.reveals: A question like "Date of birth: " with "Nairobi" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "14th March 2016", not "Nairobi".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.feedback: Read the name of the box first, then write only what it asks for.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.error: Writes the age in the date of birth box.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.cause: Confuses age with date of birth.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.reveals: A question like "Date of birth: " with "9 years" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "14th March 2016", not "9 years".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.feedback: Date of birth needs the day, month and year you were born. Age is a number.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.error: Writes a phone number in the address box.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.cause: Does not tell address from contact.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.reveals: A question like "Home address: " with "0712 345 678" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "P.O. Box 12, Kisumu", not "0712 345 678".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.feedback: An address says where you live or get letters. A phone number goes in the contact box.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.error: Writes only one name in the full names box.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.cause: Thinks the first name is enough.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.reveals: A question like "Full names: " with "Wanjiru" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Wanjiru Kamau Njeri", not "Wanjiru".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.feedback: Full names means all of your names, in the order the form asks for.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T1_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Picks a detail that sits near the answer in the text.

example.question: What was tied inside the bag?

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.cause: Reads fast and picks a nearby word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "What was tied inside the bag?" with "sand" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "rags", not "sand".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: Find the sentence that answers the question and check that the words match what is asked.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Answers from what he or she already knows.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.cause: Does not go back to the text.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "How did they travel?" with "by bus" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "by boda boda", not "by bus".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: Answer from the text, not from what you think is likely. Go back to the sentence.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Says not stated when the text does say it.

example.question: True, false or not stated: Achieng set tomatoes in heaps.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "True, false or not stated: Achieng set tomatoes in heaps." with "Not stated" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "True", not "Not stated".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: Look again. When the text says it clearly, the answer is true.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Says true when the text says something different.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.cause: Reads for the topic, not the exact detail.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "The market was in Nakuru." with "True" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "False", not "True".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: The text says something different from the statement, so the statement is false.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Says not stated when the text says something different.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.cause: Does not tell going against the text from saying nothing.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "The market was in Nakuru." with "Not stated" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "False", not "Not stated".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: If the text says the opposite, the answer is false. Not stated means the text says nothing about it.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Says true or false when the text does not say.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "Kamau scored a goal." with "True" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Not stated", not "True".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: The text does not mention it, so the answer is not stated. Do not guess from what is likely.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.error: Picks the wrong person or place for who or where.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.reveals: A question like "Who helped Kamau?" with "his teacher" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "his grandmother", not "his teacher".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.feedback: Find the sentence about the helper and check who it names.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.error: Copies a sentence from the text as the answer.

example.question: Why did Mother nod proudly?
example.wrong_answer: The woman wore a green dress.
example.correct_answer: Achieng counted carefully and gave the right change.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.cause: Does not see that the answer is not written.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.reveals: A question like "Why did Mother nod proudly?" with "The woman wore a green dress." among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Achieng counted carefully and gave the right change.", not "The woman wore a green dress.".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.feedback: An inference is worked out from clues. A sentence copied from the text is not working anything out.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.error: Picks an answer that goes against the text.

example.question: Why was Kamau sad?
example.correct_answer: He loved football and the ball burst.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.cause: Does not check the answer against the text.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.reveals: A question like "Why was Kamau sad?" with "The school was closed." among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "He loved football and the ball burst.", not "The school was closed.".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.feedback: A good inference agrees with every clue in the text.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.error: Picks an answer that goes too far.

example.question: What can you tell about the grandmother?
example.wrong_answer: She is the richest woman in town.

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.cause: Adds facts that the text does not support.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.reveals: A question like "What can you tell about the grandmother?" with "She is the richest woman in town." among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "She is kind and clever.", not "She is the richest woman in town.".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.feedback: An inference is a small step from the clues. If the text gives no clue for it, it goes too far.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.error: Picks a meaning that looks like the word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.cause: Guesses from the look of the word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.reveals: A question like "burst" with "rolled away" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "broke open", not "rolled away".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.feedback: Read the sentences around the word to find its meaning.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.error: Picks a common meaning that does not fit.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.cause: Uses a known meaning without testing it.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.reveals: A question like "heaps" with "big baskets" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "small piles", not "big baskets".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.feedback: Try the meaning in the sentence. If it does not fit, it is not the right one.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.reveals: A question like "ancient" with "very new" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "very old", not "very new".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.feedback: Read for clue words. They tell you if the word means the same as or the opposite of something.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.error: Picks a group of words that does not explain the word.

example.question: Which words help you?
example.correct_answer: the school had no money for a new one

ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.cause: Picks any phrase near the word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.reveals: A question like "Which words help you?" with "in Nyeri" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the school had no money for a new one", not "in Nyeri".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.feedback: A clue is a group of words that tells more about the hard word, not just words near it.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.error: Adds only -s to a word that ends in s, x, ch or sh.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Uses the plain -s rule for every word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "two ___ (box)" with "boxs" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "boxes", not "boxs".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: After s, x, ch and sh we add -es so that the word can be said: box, boxes; church, churches.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.error: Adds -s to a word that ends in a consonant and y.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Does not change y to i before the ending.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "three ___ (baby)" with "babys" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "babies", not "babys".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: When a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i and add -es: baby, babies.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.error: Changes y to -ies after a vowel.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "two ___ (monkey)" with "monkies" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "monkeys", not "monkies".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: When a vowel comes before the y, just add -s: monkey, monkeys; day, days.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.error: Adds -s to knife, leaf, wife and loaf.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Does not know the f to v change.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "two ___ (leaf)" with "leafs" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "leaves", not "leafs".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: Some words ending in f or fe change to -ves: leaf, leaves; knife, knives; wife, wives.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.error: Keeps the noun singular after a number.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Kiswahili does not change the noun after a number in the same way.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "I have four ___." with "book" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "books", not "book".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: After two, three, four or any number above one, the noun must be plural: four books.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Uses the regular rule for every noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "three ___ (child)" with "childs" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "children", not "childs".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: A few nouns change in their own way. The plural of child is children, and of man is men.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.error: Adds -s to a plural that is already plural.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Knows the word changes but adds -s from habit.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "Many ___ were playing. (child)" with "childrens" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "children", not "childrens".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: Children, men and women are already plural. Do not add -s.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Does not know the vowel change.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "two ___ (tooth)" with "tooths" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "teeth", not "tooths".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: Some plurals change the vowels inside the word: tooth, teeth; mouse, mice; goose, geese.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.cause: Treats every animal word as regular.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.reveals: A question like "ten ___ (sheep)" with "sheeps" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "sheep", not "sheeps".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.feedback: Sheep stays sheep. We say one sheep and ten sheep. Fish is the same.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.error: Makes a request as a demand.

example.question: You want to borrow a pen. What do you say?
example.correct_answer: May I please borrow your pen?

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.cause: Says the shortest thing that gets the pen.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.reveals: A question like "You want to borrow a pen. What do you say?" with "Give me your pen." among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "May I please borrow your pen?", not "Give me your pen.".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.feedback: A polite request starts with May I or Could you, and says please.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Your friend helps you. What do you say?

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.cause: Does not see thanks as needed.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.reveals: A question like "Your friend helps you. What do you say?" with "Okay." among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Thank you for helping me.", not "Okay.".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.feedback: When someone helps you, say thank you.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: You cannot lend your book. What do you say?
example.correct_answer: I am sorry, I cannot lend it today.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.cause: Does not know how to say no politely.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.reveals: A question like "You cannot lend your book. What do you say?" with "No. Go away." among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "I am sorry, I cannot lend it today.", not "No. Go away.".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.feedback: You can say no in a polite way: begin with I am sorry.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.error: Does not say sorry after a mistake.

example.question: You step on someone's foot. What do you say?
example.correct_answer: Sorry, I did not see you.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.cause: Does not see that sorry is needed.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.reveals: A question like "You step on someone's foot. What do you say?" with "Move." among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Sorry, I did not see you.", not "Move.".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.feedback: When you hurt or bother someone, say sorry.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.error: Puts to, -s or -ing after May I or Could you.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.cause: Thinks every verb needs "to" before it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.reveals: A question like "May I ___ in?" with "to come" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "come", not "to come".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.feedback: After May I and Could you the verb stays plain: May I come in? Could you help me?
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.error: Makes a request as a command.

example.question: Which is polite? Give me water.
example.correct_answer: Could you give me some water, please?

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.cause: Uses the command that is quick and short.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.reveals: A question like "Which is polite? Give me water." with "Give me water." among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Could you give me some water, please?", not "Give me water.".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.feedback: A polite request uses May I or Could you, and the word please.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.error: Writes Would you like with -ing or a wrong verb form.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.cause: Mixes Would you like with Do you want.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.reveals: A question like "___ you like some tea?" with "Do" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Would", not "Do".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.feedback: To offer something politely we say: Would you like some tea? The verb after like is to + the plain verb, or a noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.error: Puts the words of the request in the wrong order.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.cause: Does not move the helping word before the subject.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.reveals: A question like "Could ___ help me?" with "help you" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "you help", not "help you".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.feedback: In a request the helping word comes first: Could you help me? May I borrow your pen?
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T3_LANGUAGE_PATTERN.POLIT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.error: Picks a first aid word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: A ___ is a cloth wrapped round a cut.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.cause: Mixes up words in the same topic.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.reveals: A question like "A ___ is a cloth wrapped round a cut." with "bruise" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "bandage", not "bruise".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.feedback: Read the whole sentence and say what the gap must mean before choosing.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: A ___ is a dark mark on the skin where you were hit.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.cause: Treats the two words as the same.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.reveals: A question like "A ___ is a dark mark on the skin where you were hit." with "wound" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "bruise", not "wound".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.feedback: A wound is a cut or a break in the skin. A bruise is a dark mark under the skin.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: When you twist your ankle, it may be a ___.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.reveals: A question like "When you twist your ankle, it may be a ___." with "ambulance" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "sprain", not "ambulance".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.feedback: A sprain is a twisted joint. An ambulance is a vehicle that takes people to hospital.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.error: Reads the wrong row or column of a table.

example.question: What time does the bus to Kisumu leave?

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.cause: Looks at the nearest number instead of the row for Kisumu.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.reveals: A question like "What time does the bus to Kisumu leave?" with "10:30 am" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "8:00 am", not "10:30 am".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.feedback: Find the row for what you need, then read across to the right column.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.error: Picks a nearby detail on the notice.

example.question: Which day is the clinic closed?

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.cause: Picks the line next to the answer.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.reveals: A question like "Which day is the clinic closed?" with "Saturday" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Sunday", not "Saturday".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.feedback: Go back to the line that answers the question and check the words.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.error: Says the wrong purpose for a visual.

example.question: What is the notice for?
example.correct_answer: to tell people the time of the meeting

ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.reveals: A question like "What is the notice for?" with "to sell shoes" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "to tell people the time of the meeting", not "to sell shoes".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.feedback: Look at the title and the first line. They say what the notice is for.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_VI.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Uses I, he, we or they after a verb or a small word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Hears "Him and I" in speech and over-corrects.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "Mum gave the book to ___." with "I" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "me", not "I".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: After a verb or a small word like to, for or with, use me, him, her, us or them.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Uses me, him, us or them before the verb.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Uses the object form in a pair of names.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "___ went to the market." with "Me and Wanjiru" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Wanjiru and I", not "Me and Wanjiru".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: Before a verb, who does the action? Use I, he, she, we or they: Wanjiru and I went to the market.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Says the noun and then repeats it with a pronoun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Copies the pattern of speech where the name is said and then repeated.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "Wanjiru ___ is tall." with "she" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "no pronoun", not "she".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: Do not say the name and the pronoun together. Wanjiru is tall, or She is tall.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Says he for a girl, or she for a boy.

example.question: Akinyi is my sister. ___ is nine.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Kiswahili has one word (yeye) for he and she.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "Akinyi is my sister. ___ is nine." with "He" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "She", not "He".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: Use he for a boy or man and she for a girl or woman.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Writes my, your or her when no noun follows.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Does not tell the two sets apart.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "That bag is ___." with "my" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "mine", not "my".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: When no noun comes after, use mine, yours, hers, ours or theirs: That bag is mine.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Writes mine, yours or hers before a noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Over-uses the form that stands alone.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "This is ___ pencil." with "mine" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "my", not "mine".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: Before a noun use my, your, her, our or their: my pencil.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Thinks a belonging word needs an apostrophe, as in a name.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "The blue pen is ___." with "your's" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "yours", not "your's".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: Words like yours, hers, ours and theirs never have an apostrophe.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.error: Uses the possessive of another person.

example.question: Wafula, this book is not mine. It is ___.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.cause: Does not follow who is speaking and who is spoken to.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.reveals: A question like "Wafula, this book is not mine. It is ___." with "his" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "yours", not "his".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.feedback: Ask who owns it. The person spoken to is you, so the word is yours.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.error: Mixes up the parts of a letter.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.cause: Does not know the names of the parts.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.reveals: A question like "Which part says "Dear Amina,"?" with "closing" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "greeting", not "closing".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.feedback: The greeting comes first and starts with Dear. The closing comes at the end, for example Yours lovingly.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.error: Puts the parts of the letter in the wrong order.

example.question: Which comes first in a friendly letter?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.cause: Does not know the usual order.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.reveals: A question like "Which comes first in a friendly letter?" with "the closing" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "your address and the date", not "the closing".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.feedback: A friendly letter goes: your address, the date, the greeting, the body, the closing, your name.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.error: Leaves the comma out after the greeting or the closing.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.cause: Writes the greeting as a plain word group.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.reveals: A question like "Which is correct?" with "Dear Amina" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Dear Amina,", not "Dear Amina".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.feedback: A comma follows the greeting (Dear Amina,) and the closing (Yours lovingly,).
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.error: Writes the receiver's address at the top of a friendly letter.

example.question: Whose address goes at the top?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.cause: Copies the pattern of a formal letter.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.reveals: A question like "Whose address goes at the top?" with "the person getting the letter" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the writer", not "the person getting the letter".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.feedback: In a friendly letter, write your own address at the top. Do not write the receiver's address there.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.LET.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.error: Picks a food word that is near in meaning but wrong.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.reveals: A question like "Beans and meat give us ___." with "carbohydrates" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "protein", not "carbohydrates".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.feedback: Protein builds the body (beans, meat, eggs). Carbohydrates give energy (ugali, rice, bread).
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: ___ help us stay healthy and are found in fruits.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.reveals: A question like "___ help us stay healthy and are found in fruits." with "Fibre" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Vitamins", not "Fibre".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.feedback: Vitamins keep the body healthy. Fibre helps food move through the body.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.error: Thinks a balanced diet is one food in a large amount.

example.question: A balanced diet has ___.
example.correct_answer: all the food groups in the right amounts

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.cause: Does not know the meaning of balanced.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.reveals: A question like "A balanced diet has ___." with "only ugali" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "all the food groups in the right amounts", not "only ugali".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.feedback: A balanced diet has food from all the food groups in the right amounts.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.error: Picks another number from the text.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.cause: Does not look for the key word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.reveals: A question like "How much is a ticket?" with "60 shillings" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "50 shillings", not "60 shillings".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.feedback: Scan for the key word in the question (ticket) and read only that line.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.error: Looks for the wrong key word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.cause: Uses a word that is not the key word.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.reveals: A question like "When does the show start?" with "at 6 pm" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "at 4 pm", not "at 6 pm".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.feedback: Choose the key word that matches the question, then read the line.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.error: Reads the whole text to find one detail.

example.question: What is the name of the guide?
example.wrong_answer: a long answer from the whole text

ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.reveals: A question like "What is the name of the guide?" with "a long answer from the whole text" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Mr Otieno", not "a long answer from the whole text".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.feedback: Look for a capital letter or a number. Skip the rest.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T5_EXTENSIVE_READING.SCAN.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Picks the noun as the describing word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.cause: Does not tell what the word does in the sentence.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "The red bus stopped." with "bus" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "red", not "bus".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: An adjective describes a noun. Ask which word tells more about the bus: red.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Picks the verb as the describing word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.cause: Takes any word that adds meaning as a describing word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "The tall girl ran home." with "ran" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "tall", not "ran".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: A verb tells what someone does. An adjective tells what someone or something is like.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Picks an adverb as the adjective.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.cause: Does not separate describing a noun from describing a verb.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "The small boy walked slowly." with "slowly" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "small", not "slowly".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: Slowly tells how the boy walked, so it is an adverb. Small tells what the boy is like, so it is the adjective.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Picks a, an or the as the adjective.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.cause: Thinks any small word before a noun describes it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "Mama bought a sweet mango." with "a" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "sweet", not "a".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: A, an and the point to a noun but do not describe it. Sweet describes the mango.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Puts the shape before the size.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "She sat on a ___ stool." with "round big" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "big round", not "round big".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: Size comes first, then shape: a big round stool.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Puts the adjective after the noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.cause: Kiswahili puts the adjective after the noun.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "Amina has a ___." with "ball big" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "big ball", not "ball big".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: In English the describing word comes before the noun: a big ball.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.error: Joins two adjectives with and or a comma.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.cause: Copies the way two things are joined in speech.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.reveals: A question like "a ___ table" with "big and round" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "big round", not "big and round".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.feedback: Two describing words before a noun need no and and no comma: a big round table.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.error: Puts the end of the story at the beginning.

example.question: Which part tells how the story ends?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.cause: Does not know what each part does.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.reveals: A question like "Which part tells how the story ends?" with "the beginning" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the end", not "the beginning".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.feedback: The beginning introduces people and place, the middle tells what happens, and the end tells how it finishes.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Which tells where and when a story happens?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.cause: Uses the two words as if they meant the same.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.reveals: A question like "Which tells where and when a story happens?" with "the characters" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the setting", not "the characters".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.feedback: Characters are the people or animals in the story. The setting is where and when it happens.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.error: Places the problem at the end instead of the middle.

example.question: Where does the problem of a story usually come?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.cause: Thinks a story needs the problem last.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.reveals: A question like "Where does the problem of a story usually come?" with "at the end" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "in the middle", not "at the end".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.feedback: The problem usually starts in the middle. The end tells how it was solved.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.error: Thinks the title tells the whole story.

example.question: What does a title do?
example.correct_answer: gives a short name to the story

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.cause: Does not know the purpose of a title.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.reveals: A question like "What does a title do?" with "tells the whole story" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "gives a short name to the story", not "tells the whole story".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.feedback: A title is a short name that hints at the story. It does not tell all of it.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.NARRA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.error: Puts the sentences in the reverse order.

example.question: Put the four sentences in order.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.cause: Starts from the sentence that sounds like an ending.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.reveals: A question like "Put the four sentences in order." with "D C B A" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "A B C D", not "D C B A".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.feedback: Start with the sentence that introduces the topic and read forward.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Put the four sentences in order.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.cause: Does not check the sequence words (first, then, next).
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.reveals: A question like "Put the four sentences in order." with "A C B D" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "A B C D", not "A C B D".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.feedback: Look at words like first, then, next and finally to see the order.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.error: Chooses a detail as the topic sentence.

example.question: Which is the topic sentence?
example.correct_answer: the sentence that tells what the paragraph is about

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.cause: Picks the first sentence the eye meets.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.reveals: A question like "Which is the topic sentence?" with "a detail" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the sentence that tells what the paragraph is about", not "a detail".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.feedback: The topic sentence names what the whole paragraph is about. The other sentences give details.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T5_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.error: Picks an internet word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: The messages you receive are kept in your ___.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.cause: Mixes up the parts of an email.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.reveals: A question like "The messages you receive are kept in your ___." with "attachment" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "inbox", not "attachment".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.feedback: The inbox is where received emails are kept. An attachment is a file sent with an email.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.error: Thinks a password can be shared with friends.

example.question: A password should be shared with ___.
example.correct_answer: no one except a trusted adult

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.cause: Does not know why a password is secret.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.reveals: A question like "A password should be shared with ___." with "friends" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "no one except a trusted adult", not "friends".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.feedback: A password is secret. Share it with no one, except a trusted adult such as a parent.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.error: Replies to or trusts a stranger online.

example.question: A stranger online asks where you live. You should ___.
example.correct_answer: not answer and tell an adult

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.cause: Believes a friendly message is safe.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.reveals: A question like "A stranger online asks where you live. You should ___." with "tell him" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "not answer and tell an adult", not "tell him".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.feedback: Never give personal information to a stranger online. Tell a trusted adult.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.I.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.error: Uses much with things that can be counted.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.cause: Treats many and much as the same word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.reveals: A question like "There are not ___ chairs." with "much" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "many", not "much".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.feedback: Use many with things you can count (chairs, books). Use much with things you cannot count (water, sugar).
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.error: Uses many with things that cannot be counted.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.reveals: A question like "There is not ___ water." with "many" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "much", not "many".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.feedback: You cannot count water one by one, so use much, not many.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.error: Uses few with something uncountable, or little with something countable.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.cause: Does not link few and little to what is counted.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.reveals: A question like "We have ___ sugar left." with "few" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "little", not "few".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.feedback: Few goes with things you can count: few eggs. Little goes with things you cannot count: little sugar.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.error: Uses much in a plain positive statement.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.cause: Does not know that much is mostly kept for questions and negatives.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.reveals: A question like "She has ___ friends." with "much" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "many (or a lot of)", not "much".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.feedback: In a positive sentence we usually say a lot of or many: She has many friends.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.error: Uses any in a positive sentence.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.cause: Does not tell positive from negative sentences.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.reveals: A question like "I have ___ sugar." with "any" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "some", not "any".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.feedback: Use some in a positive sentence: I have some sugar. Use any in a question or after not: I do not have any sugar.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.cause: Keeps one word for all sentences.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.reveals: A question like "I do not have ___ money." with "some" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "any", not "some".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.feedback: After not or in a question, use any: I do not have any money. Do you have any money?
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.reveals: A question like "We have ___ for everyone." with "food enough" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "enough food", not "food enough".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.feedback: In English enough comes before the noun: enough food.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.error: Writes a lot before the noun without of.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.cause: Leaves out the small word of.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.reveals: A question like "There are ___ mangoes." with "a lot mangoes" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a lot of mangoes", not "a lot mangoes".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.feedback: A lot needs of before the noun: a lot of mangoes.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T6_WORD_CLASS_DETERMINE.S.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.cause: Starts from the last event seen.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.reveals: A question like "Which order tells the story?" with "D, C, B, A" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "A, B, C, D", not "D, C, B, A".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.feedback: Find the picture that starts the story and then follow what happens next.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.cause: Does not check what must happen before what.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.reveals: A question like "Which order tells the story?" with "A, C, B, D" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "A, B, C, D", not "A, C, B, D".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.feedback: Ask what has to happen first for the next picture to make sense.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.error: Tells the picture in the present tense when the story is in the past.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.reveals: A question like "Which sentence tells the picture?" with "Wafula picks a mango." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Wafula picked a mango.", not "Wafula picks a mango.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.feedback: A story written after the event uses the past tense: Wafula picked a mango.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.error: Picks a sentence that does not match the picture.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.reveals: A question like "Which sentence tells the picture?" with "She sold the fruit." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "She picked the fruit.", not "She sold the fruit.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.feedback: Look at what the person is doing in the picture and pick the sentence that says exactly that.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T6_CREATIVE_WRITING.PICTU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.error: Uses the plain verb for something that happened already.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.cause: Kiswahili shows the past in the verb start (nilienda), so the time word seems enough.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.reveals: A question like "Yesterday I ___ to the market." with "go" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "went", not "go".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.feedback: When the time is past, the verb must show it: Yesterday I went to the market.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.cause: Uses the regular rule for every verb.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.reveals: A question like "She ___ rice for lunch. (eat)" with "eated" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "ate", not "eated".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.feedback: Some verbs change inside: go, went; eat, ate; see, saw. They do not take -ed.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.error: Uses did with a past form.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.reveals: A question like "Did you ___ the film?" with "saw" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "see", not "saw".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.feedback: After did the verb stays plain: Did you see the film?
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.error: Uses the past form for a fact or a habit.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.cause: Thinks a story always needs the past.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.reveals: A question like "The sun ___ in the east." with "rose" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "rises", not "rose".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.feedback: For a fact or something that always happens, use the present: The sun rises in the east.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.error: Leaves out am, is or are.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Kiswahili says "anasoma" with no separate helping word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "She ___ reading now." with "reading" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "is reading", not "reading".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: An action happening now needs am, is or are before the -ing word: She is reading.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.error: Uses the wrong form of be.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Does not match the helping word to the subject.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "The children ___ playing." with "is" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "are", not "is".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: Use am with I, is with one person or thing, and are with you, we, they and plural nouns.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.error: Writes the plain verb after is or are.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Forgets that the verb takes -ing after the helping word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "He is ___ now." with "play" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "playing", not "play".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: After am, is or are, the verb ends in -ing: He is playing.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Does not drop the silent e or double the last consonant.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "She is ___ a cake." with "makeing" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "making", not "makeing".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: Drop the silent e before -ing (make, making). For short words with one vowel, double the last letter (run, running).
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.error: Uses is or are for an action that was going on in the past.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Does not follow the time words of the sentence.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "When I arrived, Mum ___ cooking." with "is" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "was", not "is".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: For something that was going on in the past, use was or were: Mum was cooking.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Does not match the helping word to the subject.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "The boys ___ running." with "was" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "were", not "was".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: Use was with I and one person or thing. Use were with you, we, they and plural nouns.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.error: Writes was or were with the past form of the verb.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.cause: Thinks the verb must also show the past.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "He was ___ his lunch." with "ate" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "eating", not "ate".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: After was or were, the verb ends in -ing: He was eating his lunch.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.error: Writes the plain verb after was or were.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.reveals: A question like "They were ___ football." with "play" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "playing", not "play".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.feedback: After was or were, the main verb takes -ing: They were playing football.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.error: Does not start a sentence with a capital letter.

example.question: Which is right? we went to the lake.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.cause: Writes the way a message is typed quickly.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? we went to the lake." with "we went to the lake." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "We went to the lake.", not "we went to the lake.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.feedback: Every sentence starts with a capital letter.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.error: Leaves out the full stop at the end of a statement.
