example.question: Which is right? Mum is at work

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.cause: Does not see where a sentence ends.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? Mum is at work" with "Mum is at work" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Mum is at work.", not "Mum is at work".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.feedback: A telling sentence ends with a full stop.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.error: Writes a capital letter in the middle of a sentence for an ordinary word.

example.question: Which is right? My Mother went to the Market.
example.wrong_answer: My Mother went to the Market.
example.correct_answer: My mother went to the market.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? My Mother went to the Market." with "My Mother went to the Market." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "My mother went to the market.", not "My Mother went to the Market.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.feedback: Only the first word of a sentence, names and I take a capital. Mother and market are ordinary words.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.error: Writes the name of a person or place with a small letter.

example.question: Which is right? we live in nairobi.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.cause: Does not see a name as special.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? we live in nairobi." with "We live in nairobi." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "We live in Nairobi.", not "We live in nairobi.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.feedback: Names of people, places and days begin with a capital letter: Nairobi, Wanjiru, Monday.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.error: Writes I as a small letter.

example.question: Which is right? Today i played football.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.cause: Types i in a phone message.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? Today i played football." with "Today i played football." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Today I played football.", not "Today i played football.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.feedback: The word I always takes a capital letter.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.error: Picks a farm word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: We ___ the maize when it is ripe.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.cause: Mixes up the steps of farming.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.reveals: A question like "We ___ the maize when it is ripe." with "plant" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "harvest", not "plant".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.feedback: Planting comes first. Harvesting is gathering the crop when it is ripe.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.cause: Treats all farm things as one group.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.reveals: A question like "Cows, goats and sheep are ___." with "crops" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "livestock", not "crops".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.feedback: Livestock are farm animals. Crops are plants grown for food.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.error: Thinks fertiliser is a pest killer.

example.question: ___ makes the soil richer so that crops grow well.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.cause: Does not know the two products.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.reveals: A question like "___ makes the soil richer so that crops grow well." with "Pesticide" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Fertiliser", not "Pesticide".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.feedback: Fertiliser feeds the soil. Pesticide kills pests.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.cause: Does not know the apostrophe marks the missing letter.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.reveals: A question like "I ___ like fish. (do not)" with "dont" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "don't", not "dont".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.feedback: The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter: do not becomes don't.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.error: Puts the apostrophe in the wrong place.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.cause: Puts it between the two words instead of where the letter is missing.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.reveals: A question like "She ___ at home. (is not)" with "is'nt" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "isn't", not "is'nt".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.feedback: The apostrophe goes where the letter was left out: is not becomes isn't, with the mark in place of the o.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.error: Writes its for it is, or it's for belonging to it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.cause: Mixes up the two words that sound the same.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.reveals: A question like "___ raining today. (it is)" with "Its" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "It's", not "Its".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.feedback: It's means it is. Its (no apostrophe) means belonging to it: The cat licked its paw.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.error: Makes a short form that does not exist.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.cause: Adds n't to every helping word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.reveals: A question like "We ___ go. (will not)" with "willn't" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "won't", not "willn't".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.feedback: A few short forms change: will not is won't, can not is can't.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.CONTRACTI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.cause: Copies speech where two negatives add emphasis.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.reveals: A question like "I do not have ___ pen." with "no" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "a", not "no".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.feedback: In English one negative is enough: I do not have a pen, or I have no pen.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.error: Writes not before the verb with no helping word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.cause: Kiswahili puts a negative in the verb itself (hapendi).
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.reveals: A question like "She ___ like milk." with "not" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "does not", not "not".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.feedback: In English use do not or does not before the verb: She does not like milk.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.error: Keeps -s or -ed on the verb after does not or did not.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.reveals: A question like "He does not ___ meat." with "eats" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "eat", not "eats".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.feedback: After does not and did not, the verb stays plain: He does not eat meat.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.error: Uses do not with am, is or are.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.cause: Uses do not for every negative.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.reveals: A question like "I ___ tired." with "do not" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "am not", not "do not".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.feedback: With am, is and are, put not after the helping word: I am not tired.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T8_WORD_CLASSES.NEGATIVE_.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.error: Uses an adjective after the verb where an adverb is needed.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.cause: Kiswahili uses the same word for both in many sentences.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.reveals: A question like "She sings ___." with "beautiful" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "beautifully", not "beautiful".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.feedback: A word that tells how someone does something is an adverb. Many adverbs end in -ly: sings beautifully.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.error: Gives the wrong kind to an adverb of time, place or manner.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.cause: Does not ask the question the adverb answers.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.reveals: A question like "Which kind of adverb is "yesterday"?" with "manner" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "time", not "manner".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.feedback: Manner answers how, time answers when, place answers where. Yesterday tells when.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.error: Uses good where well is needed.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.cause: Does not know that good is an adjective.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.reveals: A question like "He plays football ___." with "good" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "well", not "good".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.feedback: Good describes a noun (a good player). Well tells how something is done (plays well).
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.error: Adds -ly to fast, hard or late.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.reveals: A question like "The bus goes ___." with "fastly" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "fast", not "fastly".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.feedback: Fast, hard and late are adverbs already. We say runs fast and works hard.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.error: Leaves out the commas in a list.

example.question: Which is right? Mama bought rice beans and maize.
example.wrong_answer: Mama bought rice beans and maize.
example.correct_answer: Mama bought rice, beans and maize.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.cause: Reads the list as one run of words.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? Mama bought rice beans and maize." with "Mama bought rice beans and maize." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Mama bought rice, beans and maize.", not "Mama bought rice beans and maize.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.feedback: In a list, put a comma between the items. Use and before the last one.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.error: Puts a comma after the last item.

example.question: Which is right? I like mangoes, oranges, and bananas,
example.correct_answer: I like mangoes, oranges and bananas.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.cause: Thinks every item needs a comma after it.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? I like mangoes, oranges, and bananas," with "I like mangoes, oranges, bananas," among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "I like mangoes, oranges and bananas.", not "I like mangoes, oranges, bananas,".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.feedback: The last item has no comma after it. Put and before it and end with a full stop.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.error: Puts a comma between who and what they do.

example.question: Which is right? Wafula, kicked the ball.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.cause: Uses a comma as a breathing mark.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? Wafula, kicked the ball." with "Wafula, kicked the ball." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Wafula kicked the ball.", not "Wafula, kicked the ball.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.feedback: Do not put a comma between a person and what the person did. A comma is not a pause mark.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.error: Uses full stops between the items of a list.

example.question: Which is right? We saw lions. zebras. and giraffes.
example.wrong_answer: We saw lions. zebras. and giraffes.
example.correct_answer: We saw lions, zebras and giraffes.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.cause: Does not know the comma has its own job in lists.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.reveals: A question like "Which is right? We saw lions. zebras. and giraffes." with "We saw lions. zebras. and giraffes." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "We saw lions, zebras and giraffes.", not "We saw lions. zebras. and giraffes.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.feedback: A full stop ends a whole sentence. Items in one list are separated by commas.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.COMMAS.M_C.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.error: Ends a question with a full stop.

example.question: Which is right? Where is the book.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.cause: Reads the question aloud with a rising voice but writes the usual end mark.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.reveals: A question like "Which is right? Where is the book." with "Where is the book." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Where is the book?", not "Where is the book.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.feedback: A question ends with a question mark.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.error: Ends a statement with a question mark because it has a question word in it.

example.question: Which is right? I do not know where he lives?
example.wrong_answer: I do not know where he lives?
example.correct_answer: I do not know where he lives.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.cause: Sees the word where and thinks a question mark is needed.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.reveals: A question like "Which is right? I do not know where he lives?" with "I do not know where he lives?" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "I do not know where he lives.", not "I do not know where he lives?".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.feedback: A sentence that tells something ends with a full stop, even if it has a word like where in it.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.error: Ends a question with a comma.

example.question: Which is right? Are you hungry,

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.cause: Does not know a comma cannot end a sentence.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.reveals: A question like "Which is right? Are you hungry," with "Are you hungry," among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Are you hungry?", not "Are you hungry,".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.feedback: A comma never ends a sentence. A question ends with a question mark.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Which is right? What is your name

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.cause: Forgets the mark in quick writing.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.reveals: A question like "Which is right? What is your name" with "What is your name" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "What is your name?", not "What is your name".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.feedback: Every sentence needs an end mark. A question needs a question mark.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION.QUESTION_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Picks a hygiene word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: Washing your hands kills ___ that cause diseases.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Mixes up words in the same topic.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Washing your hands kills ___ that cause diseases." with "rubbish" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "germs", not "rubbish".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: Germs are tiny living things that can cause disease. Rubbish is waste.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Thinks disinfect means to make something smell nice.

example.question: We ___ the toilet with a strong cleaner to kill germs.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "We ___ the toilet with a strong cleaner to kill germs." with "perfume" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "disinfect", not "perfume".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: To disinfect is to kill germs on a surface.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: A ___ is a place to dispose of human waste.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "A ___ is a place to dispose of human waste." with "drainage" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "latrine", not "drainage".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: A latrine is for human waste. Drainage carries away dirty water.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..error: Uses but where the two parts agree.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..cause: Thinks every joining word is but.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..reveals: A question like "Ali likes tea ___ coffee." with "but" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "and", not "but".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..feedback: Use and to add one idea to another. Use but when the two ideas go against each other.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: It was raining, ___ we stayed inside.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..cause: Mixes up a reason with a result.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..reveals: A question like "It was raining, ___ we stayed inside." with "because" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "so", not "because".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..feedback: Because gives the reason. So gives the result. The rain is the reason; staying inside is the result.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..error: Uses and where the two ideas go against each other.

example.question: I wanted to play, ___ I was tired.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..cause: Uses and as the all-purpose joining word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..reveals: A question like "I wanted to play, ___ I was tired." with "and" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "but", not "and".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..feedback: When the second idea goes against the first, use but, not and.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..error: Uses and where there is a choice.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..reveals: A question like "Would you like tea ___ juice?" with "and" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "or", not "and".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..feedback: To offer a choice use or. And joins two things that are both there.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..error: Uses or where both things happen.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..cause: Does not hear the choice in or.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..reveals: A question like "Mama bought rice ___ beans." with "or" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "and", not "or".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..feedback: Or shows a choice between two things. And joins two things that are both there.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..error: Uses two joining words for one link.

example.question: Although it was late, ___ we went on.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..cause: Copies the two-word pattern of speech.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..reveals: A question like "Although it was late, ___ we went on." with "but" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "no joining word", not "but".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..feedback: One joining word is enough between two ideas. Use although or but, not both.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T10_WORD_CLASS_CONJUNCTI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.error: Writes what happened instead of what the thing is like.

example.question: Which sentence is part of a description of a market?
example.wrong_answer: Yesterday I went to the market and bought a hat.
example.correct_answer: The market is noisy and smells of fresh fruit.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.cause: Confuses a description with a story.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.reveals: A question like "Which sentence is part of a description of a market?" with "Yesterday I went to the market and bought a hat." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "The market is noisy and smells of fresh fruit.", not "Yesterday I went to the market and bought a hat.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.feedback: A description tells what something looks, sounds, smells, feels or tastes like. A story tells what happened.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.error: Uses only what can be seen.

example.question: Which sentence uses a sense other than sight?
example.correct_answer: The market smells of fresh fruit.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.cause: Thinks describing means describing how it looks.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.reveals: A question like "Which sentence uses a sense other than sight?" with "The market is big." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "The market smells of fresh fruit.", not "The market is big.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.feedback: Use all the senses: sight, hearing, smell, touch and taste.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.error: Mixes up the introduction and the conclusion.

example.question: Which part names what you will describe?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.reveals: A question like "Which part names what you will describe?" with "the conclusion" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the introduction", not "the conclusion".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.feedback: The introduction says what you are going to describe. The conclusion ends with a feeling or a last thought.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T10_CREATIVE_WRITING.DESC.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Picks a sports word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: The ___ blows the whistle to start the match.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Mixes up the people in a game.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "The ___ blows the whistle to start the match." with "goalkeeper" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "referee", not "goalkeeper".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: The referee controls the game. The goalkeeper guards the goal.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Our team won the ___ at the end of the tournament.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Does not know the two words.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Our team won the ___ at the end of the tournament." with "tournament" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "trophy", not "tournament".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: A tournament is a series of games. A trophy is the prize.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: The player on the other team is my ___.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "The player on the other team is my ___." with "teammate" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "opponent", not "teammate".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: An opponent plays against you. A teammate plays with you.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.error: Uses who for a thing and what for a person.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.cause: Does not link the question word to the kind of answer.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.reveals: A question like "___ is your teacher?" with "What" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Who", not "What".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.feedback: Who asks about a person. What asks about a thing.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.error: Uses where for a time and when for a place.

example.question: ___ do we start? At nine o'clock.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.cause: Does not listen to the answer.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.reveals: A question like "___ do we start? At nine o'clock." with "Where" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "When", not "Where".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.feedback: When asks about time. Where asks about a place. Why asks for a reason.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.error: Keeps the statement order in a question.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.cause: Kiswahili questions keep the same order with a question word.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.reveals: A question like "Where ___ going?" with "you are" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "are you", not "you are".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.feedback: In a question the helping word goes before the subject: Where are you going?
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.error: Adds do to a question that already has is, are or can.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.reveals: A question like "How ___ you?" with "do are" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "are", not "do are".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.feedback: Use only one helping word. How are you? Where do you live?
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.cause: Mixes up two words that sound the same.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.reveals: A question like "___ bag is this?" with "Who's" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Whose", not "Who's".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.feedback: Whose asks who owns something. Who's means who is.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T11_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.INT.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..error: Swaps the vowels in ie and ei words.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..cause: Does not remember which vowel comes first.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..reveals: A question like "Wanjiru is my best ___." with "freind" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "friend", not "freind".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..feedback: Check the word. Friend has ie, as in "a friend to the end". Learn it as a whole word.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..error: Spells the word as it sounds.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..reveals: A question like "We stayed home ___ it rained." with "becos" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "because", not "becos".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..feedback: Many words are not spelt the way they sound. Learn the shape: because (be-cau-se).
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..error: Leaves out a letter that is not heard.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..cause: Does not say the middle letter.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..reveals: A question like "We have a ___ at school." with "libary" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "library", not "libary".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..feedback: Say the word slowly in parts: li-brar-y. Do not leave out the r.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..error: Leaves out or changes letters in a long vowel group.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..reveals: A question like "The flowers are ___." with "beutiful" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "beautiful", not "beutiful".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..feedback: Beautiful starts with beau, as in "beautiful". Look at the word again and copy its shape.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Picks an environment word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: To ___ plastic is to make it into something new.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Mixes up words in the same topic.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "To ___ plastic is to make it into something new." with "litter" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "recycle", not "litter".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: To recycle is to make waste into something new. Litter is rubbish dropped in a public place.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Thinks pollution is a kind of plant.

example.question: ___ is the dirt that harms air, water or soil.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "___ is the dirt that harms air, water or soil." with "Compost" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Pollution", not "Compost".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: Pollution is dirt or poison that harms the air, water or soil.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Thinks conserve means to use up.

example.question: We should ___ water, not waste it.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "We should ___ water, not waste it." with "pollute" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "conserve", not "pollute".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: To conserve is to look after and use carefully.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.error: Reads a proverb as only about its animals or things.

example.question: Haste makes waste means:
example.correct_answer: doing a thing too fast can spoil it

ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.cause: Takes the words at face value.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.reveals: A question like "Haste makes waste means:" with "people who hurry waste water" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "doing a thing too fast can spoil it", not "people who hurry waste water".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.feedback: A proverb is a short saying with a lesson. Ask what it teaches people.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Slow and steady wins the race means:
example.correct_answer: keep going carefully and you will succeed

ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.cause: Does not read the whole proverb.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.reveals: A question like "Slow and steady wins the race means:" with "be fast to win" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "keep going carefully and you will succeed", not "be fast to win".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.feedback: Check the lesson against the proverb. The lesson of this one is patience.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.error: Picks a lesson that has nothing to do with the proverb.

example.question: A stitch in time saves nine means:
example.correct_answer: fix a small problem early to avoid a big one

ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.reveals: A question like "A stitch in time saves nine means:" with "sewing is hard" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "fix a small problem early to avoid a big one", not "sewing is hard".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.feedback: The lesson must fit the idea of the whole proverb.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.error: Finishes a proverb with a word that sounds right but is not.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.cause: Remembers the idea and not the exact words.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.reveals: A question like "Easy come, easy ___." with "stay" among the options.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "go", not "stay".
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.feedback: A proverb always has the same words. Say the whole saying aloud.
ENGL.G4.READIN.T12_1_INTENSIVE_READING.P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Uses the simple past form after have or has.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Does not know the past participle of irregular verbs.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "I have ___ my lunch." with "ate" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "eaten", not "ate".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: After have or has use the past participle: have eaten, has gone, have seen.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Does not match the helping word to the subject.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "She ___ finished her work." with "have" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "has", not "have".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: Use has with he, she, it and one person or thing. Use have with I, you, we, they and plural nouns.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Uses the plain verb after have or has.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Leaves out the past participle ending.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "They have ___ home." with "go" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "gone", not "go".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: After have or has the verb needs its past participle: gone, taken, written.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Uses have or has with yesterday, last week or an exact past time.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Thinks have or has is simply a past marker.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "I ___ him yesterday." with "have seen" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "saw", not "have seen".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: When the time is named (yesterday, last week), use the simple past: I saw him yesterday.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Uses the simple past for both events.

example.question: The bus ___ left before I arrived.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Does not mark which event came first.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "The bus ___ left before I arrived." with "was" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "had", not "was".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: The earlier of two past events takes had + participle: The bus had left before I arrived.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Uses have or has where had is needed.

example.question: When I got home, Mum ___ cooked.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Does not move the helping word into the past.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "When I got home, Mum ___ cooked." with "has" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "had", not "has".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: In a story about the past, use had, not have or has.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Uses the plain verb after had.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "She had ___ her homework." with "finish" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "finished", not "finish".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: After had the verb is a participle: had finished, had gone.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..error: Puts had on the event that happened second.

example.question: Which happened first? Wanjiru had left when I arrived.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..cause: Does not see that had marks the earlier event.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..reveals: A question like "Which happened first? Wanjiru had left when I arrived." with "I arrived" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Wanjiru left", not "I arrived".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..feedback: The event with had happened first. Wanjiru had left, then I arrived.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T12_WORD_CLASSES_VERB_AS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: What does every diary entry start with?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.cause: Thinks the diary is only for reading by the writer.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.reveals: A question like "What does every diary entry start with?" with "a title" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "the date", not "a title".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.feedback: A diary entry begins with the date, so you know when it happened.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.error: Writes the diary as a letter to a person.

example.question: Which is the best start of a diary entry?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.cause: Mixes up the friendly letter and the diary.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.reveals: A question like "Which is the best start of a diary entry?" with "Dear Mum, how are you?" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "Monday, 4th March. Dear Diary,", not "Dear Mum, how are you?".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.feedback: A diary is written to yourself. Begin with the date and Dear Diary, not Dear Mum.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.error: Writes about himself or herself as he or she.

example.question: Which sentence is in the right voice?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.cause: Writes as in a story told by someone else.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.reveals: A question like "Which sentence is in the right voice?" with "Wanjiru woke up early." among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "I woke up early.", not "Wanjiru woke up early.".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.feedback: A diary is about you, so write in the first person: I woke up early.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.error: Writes only a list of events, with no feelings.

example.question: What else does a diary entry have besides what happened?

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.cause: Thinks a diary is a record only.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.reveals: A question like "What else does a diary entry have besides what happened?" with "a list of names" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "how the writer felt", not "a list of names".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.feedback: A diary also tells how you felt: I was happy when we won.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_COMPOSITION.DI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Mama ___ money every month to buy a cow later.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Does not tell getting money from keeping it.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Mama ___ money every month to buy a cow later." with "earns" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "saves", not "earns".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: To earn is to get money for work. To save is to keep money for later.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: Can I ___ your pen? I will return it.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Does not tell who takes and who gives.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Can I ___ your pen? I will return it." with "lend" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "borrow", not "lend".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: You borrow when you take for a short time. You lend when you give for a short time.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Picks a money word that is near in meaning but wrong.

example.question: A ___ helps a family plan how to spend its money.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Mixes up words in the same topic.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "A ___ helps a family plan how to spend its money." with "price" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "budget", not "price".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: Read the whole sentence and say what the gap must mean before you choose.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: The ___ of the book is 80 shillings.

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Treats the money words as the same.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "The ___ of the book is 80 shillings." with "change" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "price", not "change".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: The price is what something costs. Change is the money given back.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Picks the letter beside the silent one.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Does not say the word slowly.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Which letter is silent in "knife"?" with "n" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "k", not "n".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: Say the word aloud. In knife you hear n, but not k.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Which letter is silent in "write"?" with "none" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "w", not "none".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: Some letters are written but not said. In write, the w is silent.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..error: Thinks the silent letter is always the last letter.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..cause: Has learnt silent e at the end.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..reveals: A question like "Which letter is silent in "lamb"?" with "m" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "b", not "m".
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..feedback: A silent letter can be anywhere. In lamb the b is silent.
ENGL.G4.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "The cup is ___ the table." with "in" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "on", not "in".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: On means touching the top of something. In means inside it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..error: Uses between for three or more things, or among for two.

example.question: The ball is ___ the two boys.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "The ball is ___ the two boys." with "among" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "between", not "among".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: Use between for two things and among for more than two.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: The cat is ___ the bed (hiding below it).

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..cause: Does not picture where the thing is.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "The cat is ___ the bed (hiding below it)." with "on" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "under", not "on".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: Under means below something. Behind means at the back of it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..error: Mixes up in front of and behind.

example.question: Juma stood ___ Achieng at the end of the line.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "Juma stood ___ Achieng at the end of the line." with "in front of" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "behind", not "in front of".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: In front of means before it. Behind means after it, at the back.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..error: Uses to where into (going inside) is needed.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..cause: Does not feel the idea of going inside.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "He ran ___ the room." with "to" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "into", not "to".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: Into shows going from outside to inside a place. To shows going towards it.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..cause: Mixes the place and the movement words.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "We go ___ school every day." with "at" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "to", not "at".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: After go use to: go to school. At tells where something is.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: Kiswahili influence (to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher)

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "I went ___ after school." with "to home" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "home", not "to home".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: Home needs no word before it after go: I went home.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

example.question: The goat ran ___ the road to the other side.

ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..reveals: A question like "The goat ran ___ the road to the other side." with "through" among the options.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "across", not "through".
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..feedback: Across means from one side of a flat place to the other. Through means passing in at one side and out at the other.
ENGL.G4.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASS_PREPOSITI..source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.error: Writes one consonant where there are two.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.cause: Does not hear the two letters.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.reveals: A question like "Mama drinks ___ every morning." with "cofee" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "coffee", not "cofee".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.feedback: Some words have two of the same letter together: coffee, summer, letter.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.error: Spells the word as it sounds.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.cause: Writes what the ear hears and picks a wrong vowel.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.reveals: A question like "The ___ ran into its hole." with "rabbet" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "rabbit", not "rabbet".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.feedback: Say the word slowly and then check it. Rabbit has bb in the middle.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.error: Doubles a letter that is single.

example.question: I wrote a ___ to my aunt.

ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.reveals: A question like "I wrote a ___ to my aunt." with "lettter" among the options.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.help: Have the child say both forms aloud and say why one fits: "letter", not "lettter".
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.feedback: Only some letters are doubled. Check each word: letter has tt but not three t.
ENGL.G4.WRITIN.T13_SPELLING.DOUBLE_CONSO.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher
